title: Apple Fitness Workout-Type Diversity Drop
app: COROS, Wahoo ELEMNT, TrainerRoad, Apple Fitness / HealthKit exports, Concept2 Logbook, Strava, Garmin Connect, and Zwift activity feeds via official APIs, FIT/CSV exports, and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=applefitness:workout
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats dc(workout_type) as workout_types, count as sessions by athlete _time
| where sessions>=10 AND workout_types<3
| sort workout_types
description: Uses Apple Fitness workout exports telemetry to monitor variety across logged workout types in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for months when routine diversity collapsed, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Apple Fitness workout exports data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a weekly cadence.
visualization: Monthly table of sessions versus distinct workout types.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Fitness & Activity Tracking — typical feeds: Strava API activities (`strava:activity`), Garmin Connect (`garmin:activity`), Fitbit Web API (`fitbit:activity`), Peloton workout history (`peloton:workout`), Zwift/TrainingPeaks exports..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `applefitness:workout`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=applefitness:workout`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Strava / Garmin Connect / Fitbit / Peloton / Zwift APIs and webhooks via Splunk HEC scripted inputs; GPX/FIT/CSV activity exports ingested as files..

**Author notes:** Ingest Apple Fitness workout exports data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a weekly cadence.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "applefitness:workout", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=applefitness:workout earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Apple Fitness Workout-Type Diversity Drop** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=applefitness:workout`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `sessions` (>= 10) after dc — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `athlete`, `sessions`, `workout_types`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=applefitness:workout
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats dc(workout_type) as workout_types, count as sessions by athlete _time
| where sessions>=10 AND workout_types<3
| sort workout_types
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=applefitness:workout earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, athlete, sessions, workout_types
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=applefitness:workout earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `sessions` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=applefitness:workout earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(sessions) AS p50 perc90(sessions) AS p90 perc99(sessions) AS p99 max(sessions) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.1.31: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Monthly Table Of Sessions Versus Distinct Workout Types (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `applefitness:workout` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=applefitness:workout | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1m` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1m` buckets.
